dependency_review.decision: Package first, then generic primitives, then cohesive model groups
dependency_review.evidence: Only explicit definitions/declarations plus one intact captured-Mandel-matrix LET; no model instances or solver calls at top level. The LET remains intact and moves earlier after its unchanged MAGICL prerequisites.

dependency_review.decision: Shared bridge definitions before atomic handler
dependency_review.evidence: Kirchhoff wrapper hoists only DECLAIM/DEFUN; its callee already has the original NOTINLINE/FTYPE declaration. Foreign-directory mutation remains before the intact single foreign-load/success/fallback transaction. No top-level wrapper call is introduced.

dependency_review.decision: Base -> generic protocols -> elastic -> generic objectivity -> remaining material families
dependency_review.evidence: Early protocol specializers use only base particle; thermal and communication marker classes have no material ancestors. All constitutive/lifecycle generic lambda lists precede specialized model methods.

dependency_review.decision: Shared state -> numerical tangent -> VM -> MC -> DP
dependency_review.evidence: Shared lifecycle methods specialize shared plastic state only. MC remains independent of VM; DP retains MC superclass. Each cohesive model file preserves original internal order and native backend dispatch.

dependency_review.decision: Primitives -> material law/state -> nonlocal engine -> concrete hooks at original damage component slot
dependency_review.evidence: Material law/FTYPE/INLINE declarations, especially APPLY-DAMAGE, are installed before nonlocal engine callers compile. All classes/generics were already prerequisites from particle and damage package. Concrete forward-superclass behavior remains an inherited exception.

dependency_review.decision: Explicit original package/policy preamble -> generic 2D primitives -> cohesive model file
dependency_review.evidence: Avoids compiling helpers in a package that has not yet been created; original package switches within the model file and debug/safety/speed policy are preserved.

dependency_review.decision: Seven original source files copy byte-for-byte
dependency_review.evidence: Chalk, concrete, ice, limestone, frictional damage, degradation and damage output adapter retain exact source order, declarations, package switches, CLOS ancestry and internal side effects.

declaration_policy: All original DECLAIM forms stay exact and listed per target; declarations that accompany individual functions remain before those functions in their family group.

Only explicit IN-PACKAGE and original effective optimization-policy preambles may be inserted for a new compilation file; these additions are recorded per target. No FTYPE, INLINE or NOTINLINE declaration is synthesized or deleted.
Read-time #.cl-mpm/settings:*optimise-setting* is retained, not evaluated by this planner. Fresh compile/load/catalog checks must prove policy/package changes did not alter contracts/results.

asdf_integration.system_names_and_dependency_edges: Preserve existing names/edges. Root owns cl-mpm.asd; helper never rewrites it, preserving unrelated P5 pathname changes.
asdf_integration.component_replacements: At each moved original file component, use compact_ordered_targets in order. Preserve the original component ID as a serial MODULE at its original parent pathname, containing direct owner file children; keep optional systems optional.
asdf_integration.shim_policy: Old file path becomes a file-relative forwarding loader over the same compact ordered targets. Normal ASDF loads direct owner children once; no old shim in normal component graph.
asdf_integration.runtime_boundary: cl-mpm/ext remains the owner system of shared bridge and atomic CPP transaction. Native DLL/source freezing must intercept system ownership, not historical cpp filename.
asdf_integration.metadata_caveat: P0 native component routes are retained as placement references; root changed unrelated fastmaths/linear-solver pathnames during planning. Do not restore an old entire ASD copy.

targeted_exceptions.detail: The one HANDLER-CASE contains DLL lifecycle, generic Kirchhoff/matrix/DR bindings, model-specific native wrappers and selected fallbacks. All remain byte-identical in a material backend transaction. Per-nested-definition ownership is recorded, but generic ABI definitions remain cohosted until a separately reviewed transaction-preserving split; this is not a claim of pure numerics/material separation.
The later SET-MP-DAMAGE method for PARTICLE-DAMAGE deliberately remains the winner. No new override is added or old override removed; G1 clean override elimination is not claimed.
Loading optional ice continues to replace CL-MPM/DAMAGE::APPLY-VOL-PRESSURE-DEGREDATION at the same historical load position.

Concrete is still loaded by particle before its later PARTICLE-ELASTIC-DAMAGE superclass definition from damage. Do not introduce particle -> damage -> particle merely to hide this inherited forward reference.

PARTICLE-DAMAGE contains nonlocal and material slots; relocate its intact definition into the material family while engine typed adapters retain their symbols/load order. Do not redesign superclasses/slots.
Existing C++ failure path has no VM/tangent fallback, a DP-to-MC fallback with differing argument order, and an empty viscoelastic fallback. Moving source does not validate or fix these paths.
Stubs remain in their original paths with no new ASDF registration or deletion.

no_full_joss_restart: Cancelled full Joss remains cancelled; architecture is not blocked on that run. Existing failures/cancellation and earlier passing evidence remain distinct.
